newsitem.title: TAIWAN: AT&T, Taiwan Far Eastern sign phone deal.
newsitem.headline: AT&T, Taiwan Far Eastern sign phone deal.

text.p: AT&T Corp. stepped up its pitch to enter Taiwan's lucrative mobile telephone market on Friday by offering its cross-border "roaming" services to local partner Far Eastern Group.

Under the deal, customers with mobile phones from AT&T-Far Eastern joint venture Far EasTone Telecommunications could use them in 50 countries and regions -- including the United States, Australia and most of Europe.

"It is critical for business people of Taiwan to have the ability to use their phones when they travel abroad, and we're the largest operator in the world," Scott Hooper, president of AT&T Wireless Services, said in an interview.
But AT&T has to crack the Taiwan market first.

Far EasTone, a $364 million venture, is one of 17 groups bidding for eight operation franchises in Taiwan's liberalising mobile telephone market. Far EasTone is seeking two licenses -- a northern regional one and a coveted island-wide franchise.
"If we get one of the licenses, Taiwanese customers would have access to this worldwide system, and we believe this makes us a very strong applicant for the mobile phone market," Hooper said.
Winning bids will be selected before 1997, with new services to rival those offered by state giant Chunghwa Telecom coming on line during 1997.

One major shortcoming under the AT&T plan for Taiwan customers, however, is lack of the ability to "roam" into China -- a crucial market for Taiwan but one where AT&T has yet to sign a cross-border roaming agreement.
Although mobile phones are in wide use on both sides of the Taiwan strait, Taiwan's ban on direct communications between the bitter rivals still prevents cross-strait roaming.
Competing with AT&T are U.S. rivals Sprint and Southwestern Bell, Singapore Telecom and Japan's Mitsubishi as well as Taiwan computer giant Acer and the Koo's Group conglomerate.
